sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Akanksha Power and Infrastructure Limited, NSE SME, ISIN INE0PCY01014. Research cutoff: 20 October 2026. Observed 19 October close: ₹170.20; market lot: 1,000 shares. Five-year nominal INR scenarios use a 15% equity hurdle and ₹5 lakh illustrative liquidity reference. Accounts use Indian GAAP/AS, not Ind AS. Growth, cash scoring and valuation use the constant parent scope; changing consolidated figures are cross-checks only. The 30 July allotment raises issued shares to 19,915,520, overriding the stale 19,580,520 in the October security master. Another 50,000 potential warrant shares are conservatively included without unreceived exercise cash. Evidence confidence is high on current audited parent levels, medium on historical cash classification and growth, and low on a fully reconciled group cash series. The latter is excluded rather than presented as precise. Gate details remain in the structured register. [S1][JUL][M1]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS 4.66; GQS 5.0; IAS 2.815. Factors: GOV 4; MOAT 5; REV 7; DUR 6; CAP 4; CASH 3; BAL 3; EXEC 5; EARN 6; R 1; D 3; P 2; L 5. Exact canonical weights, raw arithmetic, coverage and evidenceIDs are retained in structured audits. PersistentCASH 3 capsGrowthQuality at 5, with no factor reweighting. Forecast uncertainty is not evidence inaccuracy.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company makes APFC/PQS panels, capacitors, instrument transformers and controls, and provides distribution O&M and turnkey services. FY26 parent product revenue was ₹49.5165 crore, services/turnkey revenue ₹36.889 crore, and other operating revenue ₹0.0949 crore. The export line was zero versus ₹6.8466 crore in FY25. Product mix and reinvestment matter more than a single sales CAGR. Parent employee costs of ₹25.5467 crore also indicate labor-intensive delivery, not just equipment manufacturing. [S1]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Power-quality engineering, type tests, customer qualification and acquired TDK capacitor process capability provide moderate differentiation. Competitors offer comparable capacitor/reactive compensation systems; utility tender economics and customer concentration constrain pricing power. Shreem Electric primary product material offers capacitors/reactive compensation and turnkey utility projects, demonstrating relevant established competition; its leadership description is self-attributed, not independently verified market share. No peerP/E is imported. ProspectusFY 23 top 10 customers 86.15%; current named-customer approval does not prove diversified revenue. [PEER][RHP][S1]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Constant-parent revenue in FY23/FY24/FY25/FY26 was ₹46.0944/53.2566/77.6880/86.5004 crore. Annual additions were ₹7.1622/24.4314/8.8124 crore, and three-year CAGR was approximately 23.33%. The REV baseline of 8 is reduced to 7 for deceleration to 11.34% and incomplete price/volume evidence; medium confidence and four observations cap the score at 8. FY21/FY22 revenue of ₹74.2735/51.837 crore included the former electricity-sale franchise. The prospectus confirms that gross power sales ceased in FY23 after Tata took over the distribution business, with APIL switching to an O&M contract. Its table records power sales of ₹13.5058/12.8957 crore in FY21/FY22; an inconsistent crore label in adjacent prose does not override the table’s lakh units. This documented economic change supports using the post-franchise period, rather than silently choosing a favorable trough. Hanbit/Famous consolidation changes are not mixed into this growth series. [RHP][H25][S1]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The capacitor line was commissioned on 11 February 2026. Power-quality and grid needs offer a runway, but installation and customer approval do not guarantee paid utilization. Management lists capacity of 350,000 kVAr of capacitors, 12,000 CT/PT units, 4,500 vacuum contactors and 1,800 panels. Period, product mix and realized utilization are insufficiently specified for a mechanical volume forecast. Meter assets of ₹4.3008 crore remained in CWIP at March 31. The base case explicitly funds an additional ₹5 crore completion-cost assumption, maintenance capex of 3% of sales and additional collateral, rather than treating installed capacity as free growth. The completion assumption is doubled in a sensitivity. [S1][PRES]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Connected long-term receivables of ₹11.5578 crore, related advances of ₹1.9936 crore and guarantees of ₹2.48 crore require beneficiary and collection scrutiny. The auditor relied on management’s related-party list without independently testing completeness. Inventory submitted to lenders was LOWER than book inventory by ₹5.7867 crore in September and ₹2.4316 crore in March: this is a reporting-control weakness, not evidence of inflated collateral. March promoter ownership was 57.51%; promoters received 250,000 of July’s 335,000 conversion shares at the same ₹144 issue price. Director remuneration was ₹0.7733 crore versus ₹0.7645 crore. The FY25 AGM proposed Kayde’s appointment after Dilip & Prithvi’s tenure, so an unexplained auditor resignation is not inferred. The historical F-97 property-title issue in the prospectus contrasts with the current CARO statement that disclosed immovable-property title deeds are held by the company; a property-specific cure was not independently traced. June’s improved working-capital-day narrative must also be read alongside the transfer of connected receivables to long-term assets. [S1][H25][RHP][JUL][PRES]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Parent FY24/FY25/FY26 PAT was ₹2.6613/4.2851/5.7057 crore, reported CFO −₹20.3672/−₹2.9156/+₹12.5309 crore, and capex ₹4.1652/5.7932/31.5218 crore. Removing identifiable restricted-deposit placements and noncash deferred-tax financing produces partial CFO proxies of −₹10.2645/−₹2.9147/+₹14.2152 crore. Their three-year sum is ₹1.0360 crore against ₹12.6521 crore PAT, about 8.19%, before further classification differences. This is not claimed to be a fully reconstructed group cash series. FY26 reported parent CFO less capex is −₹18.9909 crore. Persistent weak conversion is supported by more than one growth-investment year.

Parent operating EBIT of ₹9.8527 crore excludes ₹1.3747 crore other income. At a standard 25% tax rate, NOPAT of ₹7.3895 crore divided by average equity-plus-debt of ₹103.74235 crore gives 7.12%. Incremental NOPAT of ₹2.0691 crore on ₹21.8943 crore additional capital is 9.45%. Late commissioning explains part of low returns, but future full-year depreciation and funding must still be earned.

FY25 consolidated accounts included Hanbit at 55%; FY26 includes Famous at 87%, while Hanbit falls to 23.18%. The reported ₹1.8845 crore investment cash inflow contains elimination of the prior ₹4.5 crore Famous investment, not verified sale proceeds. Parent comparative balances were recast to long-term connected receivables, while group comparatives were not similarly recast. Current connected balances are Udream ₹7.0769 crore and Noctilucent ₹4.4809 crore. Consolidated trade receivables still include ₹10.2792 crore older than six months, plus ₹0.4340 crore doubtful gross balances with ₹0.425 crore allowance. Related supplier advances also appear as loans in the audit disclosure. None of these classifications establishes collection. [S1][H25]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The parent-only base/bear/bull terminal values are ₹120.87/₹0.03/₹374.58 per share, producing five-year IRRs of −6.62%/−82.11%/+17.09%. The base entry value at a 15% hurdle is ₹60.09, conditional on funding and operating assumptions. Base initial revenue growth is 20%, EBITDA margin 16%, working capital 42% of sales and restricted collateral 22%; exit value uses 16 times operating NOPAT. Opening annual depreciation is normalized to ₹3.2 crore because the new capacitor assets only began depreciation in February.

Opening parent cash is ₹0.4312 crore plus the verified ₹3.618 crore July warrant payment, less a ₹2 crore operating reserve, ₹0.0779 crore net income-tax payable and an adverse service-tax settlement sensitivity of ₹0.4083 crore. Parent debt of ₹42.9575 crore already includes current maturities. No consolidated subsidiary cash or profit is added. Realizing all excluded investment book cost of ₹5.1402 crore would add only ₹2.57 to terminal value per share. Annual funding schedules and sensitivities are attached. [S1][JUL][M1] Interest includes 11% on opening debt plus a half-year charge on new borrowing, solved with the funding requirement. Using opening debt alone gives base terminal ₹121.24 and IRR −6.56%; the fuller financing convention gives ₹120.87 and −6.62%. R remains 1 and IAS remains 2.815, with no classification change. Model correction, 20 October 2026: our earlier model omitted opening claims. The revised reference settles ₹0.0000000 crore at opening and deducts ₹0.2761000 crore of remaining net legacy employee obligations at terminal. These are corrections to our calculations, not changes to issuer-reported data. Future service expense remains funded through forecast margins. Accelerated settlement gives base return -6.6257% versus the reference -6.6161%. BQS, GQS, IAS and classification are unchanged. [S1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The bear case requires ₹32.55 crore additional borrowing and leaves approximately ₹0.03 per share of terminal equity; the severe case requires ₹39.88 crore and exhausts modeled equity value. These amounts are funding requirements, not approved facilities. Connected receivables can fail just as utilization disappoints and lender headroom is exhausted. The service-tax dispute of ₹0.4414 crore, less ₹0.0331 crore already deposited, is explicitly stressed. TDS arrears of ₹0.0398 crore and GST demand of ₹0.0384 crore are not blindly added again to statutory current liabilities of ₹0.7626 crore. The ₹2.48 crore guarantees for Noctilucent/Udream are contingent, not additional drawn debt. The ₹5/10 crore credit-loss cases are hypothetical portfolio stresses, not asserted expected guarantee calls. [S1][S2] Credit impairment reduces opening recoverable working capital; the noncash expense is charged to PAT and added back in CFO. Funding the unchanged target closing working-capital stock captures lost collections/replacement funding once. No separate initial cash loss or extra guarantee payment is deducted. No tax shield on that hypothetical write-off is assumed.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five- and ten-times the ₹170.20 entry price require ₹851 and ₹1,702 per share. At 20 times terminal PAT and 1.996552 crore potential shares, that requires approximately ₹84.95 crore and ₹169.91 crore profits, versus current parent PAT of ₹5.7057 crore. At a 15% PAT margin, sales would need roughly ₹566 crore and ₹1,133 crore, versus ₹86.5 crore currently. This needs manyfold customer, cash and financing expansion; the new line alone does not establish a multibagger thesis. [S1][JUL][M1]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Monitor seven linked items: capacitor qualified output, paid orders and margin after February commissioning; completion and spending on the ₹4.3008 crore meter CWIP; receipts against ₹11.5578 crore connected long-term balances and ₹1.9936 crore advances; restricted deposits versus free cash and bank utilization, especially continued use above 95%; parent CFO after deposit and tax classification; remaining potential warrants and actual exercise cash; and guarantee calls, tax resolution and lender-inventory reconciliation. Persistent cash weakness despite slower sales, or inability to finance committed expansion, breaks the funded case. [S1][S2][JUL]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: capital-intensive expansion watchlist, not a demonstrated compounder or price-insensitive purchase. The dated quote is about 59.4 times parent earnings using July’s issued shares. Even substantial growth and improved margins do not meet the return hurdle in the funded base case.

All 60 market sessions were observed. Conservative median turnover of ₹31.6895 lakh implies 3.16 days to exit ₹5 lakh at 5% participation, starting at liquidity band 7. The final L score is 5 after a two-point downgrade for ESM-I, narrow PAN breadth, the ₹170,200 lot and unobserved spread/depth. The stronger 20-session median is not substituted for the slower 60-session capacity. October 19 REG1 indicators, effective for the next trading session on October 21, also flag P/E above 50 and generic irregular SME trading. These flags do not invent missing market sessions. A lower price cannot cure unfinanceable growth. [S1][M1][REG1][REGFMT]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Sources include primary annual reports, prospectus history, July allotment, June presentation/results, official market data and a competitor’s product description. The September 15 CRISIL rationale was read earlier; a refresh attempt returned HTTP 406. Its broader Hanbit-group perimeter is not combined mechanically with audited parent data. Remaining material questions are the exact group deconsolidation cash bridge, actual connected-party receipts, residual warrant expiry, detailed meter completion budget, current credit/guarantee capacity and live execution depth. Parent-led scoring is deliberate: non-operating investments receive zero incremental base value with a recovery sensitivity, rather than invented consolidated precision. [S1][H25][RHP][S2]

valuation.status: Parent-only conditional model; changing consolidated perimeter not treated as a comparable cash series
assumption_basis: Use constant parent 86.5004 crore revenue, debt 42.9575 crore and cash 0.4312 crore. Do not add consolidated subsidiary cash/profit to parent valuation. Famous/Vigyam/Hanbit investments receive zero incremental base value, with 5.1402 crore book-cost realization sensitivity; this is conservative modeling, not a claim they are worthless.

July 30 primary allotment adds 335000 shares and 3.618 crore cash. Official October 19 security master capital is stale. March warrant deposit 1.386 crore implies 385000 original warrants at 36 rupees paid; after 335000 conversion,50 k potential shares conservatively included without unreceived 0.54 crore cash. Residual expiry/conversion status is not conclusively verified.

Deposits 11.4937+11.0372=22.5309 crore are restricted, not surplus net cash. Model funds additional collateral as revenues grow; ongoing collateral is not released at terminal valuation. Connected long-term receivables 11.5578 crore remain in economic WC despite balance-sheet reclassification.

Income tax net payable is excluded from operating provisions and settled once. Service-tax appeal 44.14 lakh less 3.31 lakh paid is an immediate adverse-settlement sensitivity, not expected outcome. Disclosed TDS 3.98 lakh/GST 3.84 lakh not blindly added again to statutory current liabilities.

FY 26 parent capex 31.5218 crore already spent. Model completion capex 5 crore in year 1 is an explicit estimate for remaining meter/commissioning work, not a disclosed commitment; sensitivity doubles it. Annual maintenance 3% sales base,4% bull,2.5% bear. Existing 4.3008 crCWIP is not charged a second time.

Full-year opening depreciation 3.2 crore is an analyst normalization above FY 26 parent 1.3386 crore, because capacitor assets began depreciation onlyFebruary 11. Additional capex depreciated 6% using half-year convention. FY 26 small depreciation runrate is not perpetuated.

Base 20/20/15/15/12% sales growth and 16% EBITDA margin require successful capacitor ramp above FY 26 parent 12.94% margin. Bull 21%/fast growth is ambitious; bear 11%/slow growth and severe 7% show downside. No unverified orders or pipeline automatically booked as sales.

Interest is 11% on opening debt plus a half-year 11% charge on new borrowing, solved iteratively with the cash funding need; no same-year interest saving on repayments is assumed. Tax is 25% of positive pre-impairment PBT, without an assumed tax benefit on receivable write-offs; dividends are zero. New debt is required funding, not an available bank facility; CRISIL 99% utilization makes funding feasibility material. No unapproved equity financing is assigned a free share price.
Terminal 12/16/20 x operating NOPAT,severe 10 x are analyst scenarios, not market peer multiples. Return formula(terminal/170.2)^(1/5)-1;15% hurdle entry=terminal/1.15^5.

Credit-loss stresses are noncash impairments of opening economic receivables, not separate cash obligations: reduce opening recoverable working capital, charge PAT and add the noncash write-off back in CFO, then fund the target closing working-capital stock. This creates lost collections/replacement funding once, without an immediate second cash payment. No guarantee call is additionally charged.

Opening current claims settle once. Remaining net noncurrent legacy employee obligations are deducted from terminal equity, not assigned an invented legal maturity. Future employee service expense is assumed cash-funded through forecast operating margins; it is not added back. The terminal deduction covers only the legacy balance not otherwise paid. Accelerated settlement is a timing sensitivity, not a predicted exit schedule. FY26 parent note7: noncurrent unfunded gratuity ₹27.61 lakh. Current employee/gratuity provisions remain in WC.
